assignment: When people ask for advice, they sometimes talk to more than one person. Explain why seeking multiple opinions can help someone make a better choice. Use specific details and examples in your response.
essay_1:
I think you should ask more then one person before you make a big choice. I know this because of my cousin Dana. She is a nurse and last year she had to decide if she was going to quit her job and take a travel nurse job in Arizona. She asked like five people what they thought. At first I thought she was wasting time and was just scared to pick. But then I saw it really helped her so I changed my mind.

My first reason is one person doesn't know everything. Dana's mom told her to stay because the hospital has good benefits. Thats true but her mom never did a travel job. A lady Dana works with did two of them. She told Dana stuff nobody else knew, like you have to pay taxes on the housing money and its hard to make friends when you move every thirteen weeks. So everybody only knew a little part and Dana needed all of it.

My second reason is people want different things. Her mom wanted her to stay close to home. The recruiter gets paid more if Dana signs up. Her best friend said she missed her already and she didn't even leave yet. They were not lying, but they all had there own reason for saying what they said. If Dana only listened to the recruiter she would only hear the good stuff. When she heard all five of them she could tell what was a fact and what was just what that person wanted.

My third reason is if people who don't agree on anything all say the same thing, then it is probably right. Almost everybody told Dana to read the part in the contract about canceling. She read it and it said the company could end her job with only one week notice. She made them change it to two weeks.

Also asking people is not the same thing as letting them decide for you. Dana still picked for herself. She didn't even do what her mom said. She took the job and she kept her old license just in case. She came back eight months later and she had money saved up and she was happy she did it.

So in conclusion one opinion is kind of like a guess. A lot of opinions is more like a map, because you can see more of where your going.
essay_2:
When my cousin Dana was deciding whether to leave her nursing job for a travel contract in Arizona, she asked five people what they thought. At first I thought she was just stalling. Then I watched how it went, and it showed me why asking around is a smart thing to do before a big choice.

The first reason is simple. One person can only know some things. Dana's mom told her to stay because the hospital had good benefits. That was true. A coworker who had done two travel contracts knew things her mom could only guess at. She explained how housing money is taxed and what it is like to move every thirteen weeks. Each person had one piece of the picture, and Dana needed all of them.

Second, every person who gives advice wants something, and hearing a lot of them lets you see it. Her mom wanted her close to home. Her recruiter got a bonus if she signed. Her best friend loved hanging out with her and said so. None of them lied, but each one had a reason to lean one way. The recruiter alone would have told her only the sunny, fun, exciting parts and left out the rest. With five opinions side by side, Dana could tell which points were facts and which were wishes.

Third, when people who want different things all say the same point, that point is probably strong. Almost everyone told Dana to read the cancel part of the contract slowly. She did, and she found the agency could end the job with one week of notice. That was not fair to her. She asked for two weeks and got it.

Asking a lot of people is different from letting them vote. Dana still made the choice herself. The talks gave her a list of questions to ask and a clearer idea of what she was risking. She took the contract and kept her old license active just in case. She came back eight months later with savings, a proud smile, and great stories.

One opinion is only a guess. A few opinions, when you compare them side by side, work more like a map. I think that is the best and safest way to make a big choice, and I am glad Dana showed me.
